ideas.hypothesis: After a company raises its forecast or reports results above expectations, the price keeps drifting in the direction of the news for days because investors under-react to earnings information.
ideas.rule: Entry: a headline on the decision day that names the company and says it raised its forecast/guidance/outlook or beat results expectations, AND d1 >= +2% (the market confirms the news as positive), AND entry cost <= 1.5%. Horizon 10 trading days; exit at horizon or the -8% stop. Analyst rating/target changes and regulatory approvals do not count.
ideas.source: Bernard & Thomas (1989), Post-Earnings-Announcement Drift; Chan, Jegadeesh & Lakonishok (1996), Momentum Strategies
